sn22.76:2.4: On the nine abodes of beings, see AN 9:24.
sn22.76:6.2: MN 53 identifies the seven true dhammas as conviction, shame, compunction, learning, persistence, mindfulness, and discernment. See also, AN 7:63. These seven dhammas should not be confused with the True Dhamma, the Buddha’s teaching as a whole in its unadulterated form.
sn22.76:7.1: These treasures could be either the seven factors for awakening or the seven sets of qualities that constitute the wings to awakening. See SN 46:52 and AN 8:19.
sn22.76:7.2: The training in heightened virtue, heightened mind (concentration), and heightened discernment. See AN 3:87–88.
sn22.76:8.1: The ten-factored path of the arahant. See MN 117.
sn22.76:8.2: Usually nāga denotes a great serpent or great elephant, but it can also mean a great human being. See AN 6:43.
